patch_description:
Diagnosis: across the entire 0.72 family, slope_changes (20.40), false_reversals (14.20) and smoothness_score (0.50) have never moved — velocity clamps, Whittaker polish, adaptive-Q passes and reversal damping all bound the *first* difference only. `_velocity_clamp` limits each step to |Δy| ≤ 2|v|+slack but permits alternating +limit/−limit steps; those alternating-budget steps are pure second-difference (curvature) outliers and they are exactly what registers as the ~20 surviving slope changes. No current stage constrains curvature.

Edit: add `_curvature_clamp`, a zero-phase second-difference limiter applied immediately after `_velocity_clamp` (before the reversal damp). It clamps |y[k+1] − 2y[k] + y[k−1]| to 1.5× the robust MAD scale of the *output's own* second differences — self-scaling: genuinely curved dynamics set the MAD, so the limit sits above typical true curvature and passes it, while ripple riding quiet/straight segments lies far above the MAD and is folded onto the local linear continuation (alternating ±budget steps become straight runs, eliminating their sign flips). The limit is enforced in mirrored forward/backward sweeps (forward adjusts the trailing sample k+1, backward adjusts the leading sample k−1), so the operation adds zero group delay — lag_error and responsiveness_score are untouched. It reuses the proven guard pattern from `_velocity_clamp`: 4 attempts with budget doubling, accepting only if corr ≥ 0.97 against the pre-clamp signal, otherwise identity fallback — this protects correlation/accuracy on highly curved or adversarial inputs. Cost is two O(n) sweeps, the same complexity class as the existing clamps, so efficiency_score (~1.0) and execution_time are preserved. Expected effect: slope_changes and false_reversals drop, smoothness_score rises, with zero-phase operation keeping lag_error, responsiveness, and correlation intact.
